Presentation choice, stable reconstruction

One selected output

The operator chooses which recorded camera supplies the selected diagram and its matching joint overlay and source context. The selected camera is identified explicitly. Missing, stale or unresolved selected input produces an unavailable state rather than silently displaying another camera.

The selection is a display preference. It does not change the reference/supporting roles, source pairing, reconstructed XYZ, calibration, rig association or player ownership.

Operator diagnostics stay available

Both original camera observations, the rig map, accepted-joint information and rejection reasons remain available for diagnosis. A separate display window follows the same selected camera and recorded sample; closing it returns the output to the operator workspace.

The preference survives reload when local storage is available. Physical planning keeps synthetic output separate, and none of these controls starts acquisition.

This is a camera-free presentation change. The selected source is a recorded synthetic view from the existing solver fixture, not a live RGB camera stream. Physical XYZ and maze input remain unavailable.

Review ratings concern the declared synthetic presentation scope and reported checks. They do not certify physical calibration, exposure timing, live capture, participant identity or latency.

Before and after, served locally

Before screenshots use the rig entry, stylesheet and renderer from merged main commit 145195aa21d3ea4f5fa8ceb077d2ccec0814583b with current shared imports and the same recorded solver fixture. After screenshots use the current real Vite-served application. All observations and device names are synthetic; there is no camera footage.

Remaining physical and browser limits

The existing rig experiment does not acquire two live cameras, calibrate them or verify exposure synchronization and cross-view identity. A live implementation still needs device-scoped capture ownership, bounded pairing, source timing, calibrated transforms, explicit association/recovery and independent physical accuracy/latency evidence. A display preference cannot supply those gates.

Popup behavior follows browser policy: a browser can open a tab or block a window. The inline output must remain usable, and closing a separate window must not restart capture or reconstruction. Preference persistence depends on local storage availability; blocked storage retains the current page’s selection.

Synthetic source-time checks describe recorded evaluation time. They do not turn playback into a live exposure measurement or prove camera performance. No participant data, credentials or real device identifiers are included.

Self-contained static HTML generated by scripts/displayed-camera-report.mjs. CSS and screenshots are embedded; no external rendering assets. Synthetic examples only. Date uses Asia/Shanghai.
